Allen is the highest position within an esfera: a representative of its interests at the High Table. Each of the eleven esferas has exactly three allens regardless of its population, which is why the allens of the Three Bulls are considered disadvantaged compared with those of the smaller esferas (ch. 1, 7).

What is known about allens (ch. 3–34)

  • Prim-allen. In the novel, this is the title of an esfera’s leading allen: Filippe di Berro is prim-allen of Art (ch. 3), and Fatima Ir-Reya is prim-allen of Law (ch. 28). Her bracelet is white gold with a diamond feather of the mirna Iolanta. Chapter 22 also mentions the prim-allens of Law and Shadow, whom Carlos el Niña knows.
  • Influence. Fatima, for example, oversees the legal professionals of Law whom the factory owners hire; Mor believes that for the Reformists to win, they must persuade Fatima to forbid her lawyers from representing the factory owners (ch. 20). General Deserey addresses her as “ma donna,” a formula used when requesting a great favor (ch. 28).
  • Vulnerability. Each year, the Table expels its worst allen. Filippe has held his place for six years (ch. 3); Fatima fears that she will not be spared during the purge (ch. 28).
  • The ambitious. The industrialist Maduro aspires to become an allen (ch. 34); in ch. 13, Alvaro demands that only one of Craft’s three allens should be a factory owner.

Allens in the story (ch. 3, 24–28)

Alvaro happens to become Fatima’s lover without knowing that she is an allen of Law (ch. 24–28). When he finds out, he accuses her of deceiving him; Fatima replies that she knew about him from the beginning and was checking whether he was Filippe’s spy. The commission for a book about the heroes of Solanta comes from Filippe (ch. 3). See also High Table, Esferas.
